profile.stagger_pattern: Two classes, both at-large and unnumbered. Class A = 4 seats elected 2016, 2020, 2024, 2028. Class B = 3 seats elected 2018, 2022, 2026. Elections are held at the AUGUST primary; under A.R.S. 9-821.01(D) a candidate receiving a majority is elected outright, and every Sahuarita council seat 2016-2026 was decided in August - the town appears on NO November general canvass in the window. Winners take office at the first regular council meeting after the county canvasses the November general election (documented as 2024-11-18 for the 2024 class; December for earlier cycles). Mayor and Vice Mayor are chosen by the council from among its own members at that same meeting, for two-year terms.
profile.election_month: August (primary; decided outright, no November municipal contest)

run_log.detail: Registry's Arizona entry is CORRECT on every point tested. pima.gov/2865/Election-Results is fully open to plain curl, robots permits. But the page is the NEW CivicPlus platform: results 2022-2026 hang off content.civicplus.com/api/assets/{uuid}, while 2010-2021 sit in embedded article JSON pointing at oldcms.pima.gov/UserFiles/Servers/Server_6/File/Government/... The ?contentId= query is client-side only - fetching it returns the identical page - so the older years must be scraped out of the preloadedWidgetData blob in the page source (unescape \/ and \" first). One dead lead found and recorded: http://www.pima.gov/electionresults/{YYMMDD}_Results.XML (linked from the page as 171107C_Results.XML) returns an identical 205,014-byte soft-404 for every date tried. Registry's 'do NOT try sahuarita.suiteonemedia.com' was not tested - taken as read.

sahuaritaaz.gov/265/Election-Information: 'The Town Council has seven elected members who each serve four-year staggered terms. One member is chosen as Mayor. One member is chosen as Vice Mayor.' Council-manager. Confirms 2026 = three seats, 2028 = four seats. THE A.R.S. 9-821.01(D) TRAP IS LIVE AND FULLY CONFIRMED: Sahuarita council contests appear in the Pima County AUGUST PRIMARY canvass for 2016, 2018, 2020, 2022, 2024 and 2026, and appear in NO November general canvass in any of those years (checked g2016, g2018, g2020, g2022, g2024 - 'Sahuarita' occurs only as a place name in vote-center and school-district tables). The Aug 2020 GV News report states the winners 'gave the winners enough votes to avoid a run-off in November's general election.' Anyone recording a November gap for Sahuarita would have manufactured 5 spurious cycles.

All six cycles sourced from Pima County official canvasses, extracted locally with pdftotext -layout (no summarizer in the trust path). 2016-08-30 VOTE FOR 4: Hicks 2,930 / Skelton 2,874 / Lusk 2,728 / Bracco 2,293 (over Housley 2,010, Sparks 1,977). 2018-08-28 VOTE FOR 3: Murphy 3,258 / Egbert 2,726 / Zimmerman 2,715 (over Nastase 2,616, Huber 2,102, Miramontes 1,427 - Zimmerman beat Nastase by 99 votes). 2020-08-04 ran TWO contests: '4 YEAR TERM Vote For 4' Hicks 5,402 / Lusk 4,694 / Bracco 4,168 / Davis 4,090 (over Malott 3,198, Teso 2,141) and '2 YEAR TERM Vote For 1' Morales 4,565 def. Huber 2,748. 2022-08-02 also TWO contests: 'Vote For 3' Murphy 4,856 / Morales 4,703 / Egbert 4,350 (over Rodriguez-Nastase 3,470) and 'Vote For 1' Priolo 6,521 unopposed. 2024-07-30 'Vote For 4' with exactly four candidates, all elected: Gillespie 5,456 / Priolo 5,236 / Lisk 5,146 / Lytle 4,851. 2026-07-21 'Vote For 3': Morales 3,885 / Murphy 3,837 / Hundal 3,397 (over Cubillo 2,970, Earl 2,583) - these three take office at the first meeting after the Nov 2026 canvass, i.e. AFTER this snapshot, so they generate no 2026 tenure rows. Chelsea Hundal will replace Kara Egbert.

Sahuarita publishes TRUE ACFRs (introductory section with a photo 'Mayor and Council' page) at sahuaritaaz.gov/DocumentCenter/View/{id}, FY2019=4956, FY2020=6361, FY2021=7162, FY2022=8597, FY2023=10080, FY2024=11908, FY2025=13247. Each carries the verbatim structural statement 'Residents elect seven council members. The Town Council appoints a mayor and vice mayor from the seven elected officials.' The officials page gives a full 7-name June-30 snapshot for FY2019, FY2021, FY2022, FY2023, FY2024, FY2025 - this was the spine of the reconstruction and it independently caught BOTH 2019 appointees. FY2020 is the one exception: it has the transmittal letter but NO officials page (bracketed by FY2019 and the Aug 2020 canvass, so no loss). Extraction quirk worth recording: the FY2022 officials page has two names stored ROT47-shifted in the PDF text layer - '8YJ[JS,NQQJXUNJ' and ')NFSJ5WNTQT' decode to 'Steven Gillespie' and 'Diane Priolo'. AgendaCenter is a dead end here: /AgendaCenter/ViewFile/Minutes/_MMDDYYYY-N returns HTTP 200 with a CivicPlus SIGN-IN page, ArchivedMinutes 404s, the dated search endpoint returns nothing, and /Archive.aspx has no links. robots.txt disallows /Search, so the CivicPlus site search was not used.

SIX mid-term changes found, all dated, none of them visible in any election result. gvnews.com (Green Valley News / Sahuarita Sun) is fully fetchable to plain curl INCLUDING its site search at /search/?q=...&s=start_time&sd=desc&t=article&nsa=eedition - zero WebSearches were needed. Article bodies are ROT47-obfuscated for non-subscribers but the lede is plain text and the body decodes cleanly with a 6-line ROT47 pass. (1) Dalia Zimmerman (elected Aug 2018) announced she was leaving; honoured at the 2019-05-28 meeting. (2) Lynne Skelton resigned effective 2019-06-10, term would have run to 2020. (3) Both seats stayed VACANT through the summer; 24 people applied, and Simon Davis and Erik Dahl were appointed and sworn in at the 2019-08-26 regular meeting - 'They must run for re-election in 2020, when five of the seven council seats will be open,' which is exactly what the Aug 2020 canvass shows (4+1). (4) Erik Dahl resigned in late April 2020 after discovering A.R.S. bars a state employee from holding paid elective office; he also withdrew from the 2020 ballot, and Mayor Murphy chose to run the summer with six members rather than appoint. (5) Melissa Hicks resigned effective 2022-02-01; because that was more than 30 days before the 2022-04-04 nomination deadline the unexpired term went on the ballot, which is why a lone 'Vote For 1' Sahuarita contest appears in the Aug 2022 canvass - Diane Priolo was appointed in June 2022 'serving up through the primary' and then won it unopposed. (6) Gil Lusk resigned in March 2022, INSIDE the 30-day window, so his unexpired term was NOT balloted - Steven Gillespie was chosen 3-2 over Teodoro Teso from six applicants and sworn in at the 2022-06-27 meeting for the remainder of Lusk's term to 2024. The 2020 and 2022 'two-year term' contests are the structural tell the brief describes, and following them backwards is what exposed changes 1, 2, 5 and 6.

MAYOR TRAP HANDLED - and the trap is real here: in 2018 the top vote-getter WAS Murphy, so reading the ballot top as mayor would have been accidentally right for the mayoralty and wrong for the vice mayoralty, and in 2022 the election-night tally reported by GV News had Deborah Morales AHEAD of Murphy (3,478 to 3,470) even though the final canvass reversed them (Murphy 4,856, Morales 4,703) - so a top-of-the-poll reading taken on election night would have installed the wrong mayor. Mayor and Vice Mayor are recorded as rows SEPARATE from the holders' council seats. Evidence chain for continuity: GV News reports the council 're-elected Tom Murphy to another two-year term as mayor Monday night and selected Kara Egbert as vice mayor. She succeeds Melissa Hicks' at the December 2018 organizational meeting ('The council's next meeting is Jan. 14' - Jan 14 2019 was a Monday, and Dec 10 2018 was the second Monday, matching the town's 2nd/4th-Monday schedule). A 2022 GV News piece states 'Murphy has been on the council since 2013; he was appointed mayor in 2016 and has held the position ever since' and 'Egbert was elected to the council in 2009, and again in 2013. She was appointed as vice mayor in 2018.' The ACFR officials pages then show Murphy=Mayor and Egbert=Vice Mayor at 06/30/2019, 06/30/2021, 06/30/2022, 06/30/2023, 06/30/2024 and 06/30/2025, and sahuaritaaz.gov/274/Town-Council shows the same pair today (2026-08). Every biennial re-selection (Dec 2020, Dec 2022, Nov 2024) is therefore bracketed on both sides; they are recorded as one continuous tenure each rather than four rows. Seat-count sanity: 7 in every ACFR and on the current roster, constant across the window. Day-of-week check: 2019-08-26, 2022-06-27 and 2024-11-18 are all Mondays, consistent with the town's Monday meeting schedule; 2026-07-21 (the primary) was a Tuesday. Homonym check: no surname collisions; 'Kim Lysk' in the FY2024/FY2025 ACFR is a misspelling of the canvass's 'LISK, KIMBERLY' (same e-mail stem klysk@, same seat) and is recorded as a name variant, not a second person.

CONTRADICTION FOUND AND RESOLVED. The ACFR officials pages give Gillespie the phone extension that had been Melissa Hicks's (7143) and Priolo the one that had been Gil Lusk's (7142), which suggests Gillespie took Hicks's seat and Priolo took Lusk's. Three independent GV News reports say the opposite and are unanimous: the six-applicant pool was explicitly 'to fill a vacancy left by former Sahuarita Councilmember Gil Lusk'; 'Gillespie... will fill the remainder of Gil Lusk's term, which expires in 2024'; and 'Diane Priolo, who ran unchallenged and was appointed to the vacant seat of council member Melissa Hicks in June'. The statutory logic corroborates the news: Hicks's seat WAS balloted in Aug 2022 (>30 days before the nomination deadline) and Lusk's was NOT (he resigned in March), which only works if Priolo held Hicks's seat and Gillespie held Lusk's. Phone extensions are reassigned and are not evidence. Seats 5 and 7 are labelled per the news account.

56 seat-years (7 seats x 8 years) plus 16 mayor/vice-mayor seat-years, all sourced, zero gaps. NOTE ON SEAT LABELS: Sahuarita's seven seats are at-large and UNNUMBERED - the town assigns no ward, district or position number. 'At-Large Seat 1'..'At-Large Seat 7' are analytic labels assigned here by term-class and succession lineage so that the panel yields seven distinct rows per year; they are stable across the window but are not official designations. Seats 1-3 are the three-seat class (2018/2022/2026), Seats 4-7 the four-seat class (2016/2020/2024). NOTE ON START DATES: 2024-11-18 is documented by the town ('Sworn In: November 18, 2024'). 2018-12-10 is derived from the reorganization article plus the 2nd/4th-Monday schedule. 2016-12-12, 2020-12-14 and 2022-12-12 are the corresponding second Mondays in December, applying the town's own stated rule ('sworn in during the first meeting following the Nov. 5 general election', 'the first meeting after the general election is canvassed by the county, likely in December'); they are approximate to within a few weeks and NO panel year turns on them - every one of them falls in the same calendar year as its election. 2020-04-29 (Dahl) and 2022-03-31 (Lusk) are month-level dates reported as 'last Wednesday' and 'resigned in March' respectively; both are recorded at medium confidence. Seat 3 was vacant 2019-05-28 to 2019-08-26 and again 2020-04-29 to 2020-12-14, and Seat 4 was vacant 2019-06-10 to 2019-08-26; these are partial-year vacancies inside seat-years that ARE sourced by the adjacent tenures, so per the brief they are caveats in run_log and NOT gap rows.
